newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ERA says uranium mine ruling delayed.
newsitem.headline: ERA says uranium mine ruling delayed.

text.p: Energy Resources of Australia Ltd (ERA) said on Friday the federal government had delayed until August 22 a decision on whether the company can proceeed with development of its Jabiluka uranium mine in the Northern Territory.

"This extension gives the minister for the environment 24 more days (over and above the 42-day legislative period) to carefully consider all of the issues covered in the Jabiluka environmental impact statement, ERA said.
ERA is 68.4-percent owned by miner North Ltd.
Construction at Jabiluka is scheduled to start in May 1998, with production commencing around 2000.
ERA is still in negotiations with some Aboriginal claimants who have challenged the validity of the Jabiluka mining lease in federal court, saying it was improperly granted.

ERA currently produces about 7.5 percent of the world market for uranium but hopes to lift that figure to nine percent to capture more business from civil nuclear power-generating plants, North Managing Director Campbell Anderson told Reuters earlier this week. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
